text: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how we work. One of the biggest effects is automation, where AI handles repetitive tasks like data entry, scheduling, or answering common customer questions. This frees up employees to focus on more creative and complex problems. Beyond that, many companies now use AI-powered productivity tools, such as smart email assistants or project managers that track progress and suggest improvements. However, the goal is not to replace people entirely. Instead, the best results come from human-AI collaboration—AI provides analysis and speed, while humans bring judgment and empathy. Of course, this shift means some jobs will change or disappear, but new roles will also emerge. Workers can prepare by learning to use these tools and developing skills that machines cannot easily copy, like leadership and emotional intelligence.
